analysis:
All three changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/...). No production source, protocol, key, attestation or authorization code changed, so no production trust boundary behavior regresses.

1) Fixtures/ClusterRuntime/glm-5.3-flash-dev-branch17.json is a new static JSON of digests, parity qualifications and a pair_serving_grant for a dev-branch build. It holds only public SHA-256 values, with no secrets. It is not under production paths; its use as a test fixture is unverified in the supplied evidence. Whether any non-test loader or release lane could ingest it is not shown here. Its permissive request_envelope values (1048576 tokens, video/vision true for tensor_parallel) and the 'promotable: true' flags could matter only if the file were consumed as real qualification evidence. Nothing visible indicates that, so this is noted for the integration pass rather than reported as a finding. The fixture does not touch A-016/A-017 durable qualification state.

2) ClusterApprovalFixture.swift (head lines 32-158) adds a Shape enum (pipeline or qwen27TensorParallel with optional tensor assistant), a capability variant for Qwen 27B with supportedGenerationModes, and conditional generationMode/tensorAssistant keys in saved setup JSON. This is test scaffolding using fake hash values (repeated characters) and local temp roots with 0700/0600 permissions, consistent with existing practice.

3) ClusterApprovalServiceStartTests.swift (head lines 11-61, 116-155) adds tests that a supervised service's member part must not beat into the service's own heartbeat file, and that an empty heartbeat env value stays empty. This tests an availability-oriented behavior (spurious supervisor restarts) and does not weaken a control. The production implementation (ClusterService.partEnvironment, ClusterServiceAgent.partHealthPath) is outside the supplied evidence, so I cannot verify it here.

No threat-model updates appear necessary for these test-only changes. Remaining questions for integration: confirm the JSON fixture is referenced only by tests and that the production changes enabling tensor_parallel/tensorAssistant are reviewed elsewhere in the PR.
